categories.finding: Five async_reg declarations are ignored by Quartus 18.1. Two physical stages exist in RTL; these ignored attributes provide no Quartus metastability-identification evidence.

14 warnings: ten referencePaired int-to-signed15 conversions are bounded by native coordinates and products at most 12*512=6144; i2c SDA zero reduces to one bit and the 3-bit counter intentionally wraps modulo 8; vendor VGA reset counts 797 and 524 fit ten bits.
Both undriven read outputs are explicitly disconnected and read_not_write is tied 0 in the sole active instantiation. SCCB readback is not implemented or validated.

fsm_output supplies complete defaults for sda_set, scl_idle and write_ready before its case. Missing default case item therefore does not infer a latch; unused state encodings retain those safe defaults.
Eight frame_buffer multi-bank bookkeeping registers are unused because the active instance has BUFFERS=1; two reader grid variables are assigned but unused. They are removed, not functional storage.

Quartus adds pass-through logic to preserve the synchronous read/write RTL semantics of the one-row mask memory. This is not proof of final timing; retained RTL replay exercises the actual cleanup algorithm.

Pixel FIFO: reads are gated by !empty, writes by !full, using delayed Gray pointers, so legal traffic after a common reset epoch never reads and writes the same live address; resetting only one domain is outside its contract. VGA framebuffer: BUFFERS=1 intentionally allows asynchronous read/write overlap, so moving-scene tearing and a colliding pixel are not defined. Recognition and GRAB ownership do not consume VGA RAM.

Four connectivity-warning hierarchies are two Intel altsource_probe instances, disabled PLL optional control ports, and the VGA controller empty port. No custom perception transaction input is left unspecified. Actual JTAG enumeration and VGA are still hardware acceptance requirements.

Unused GPIO remains undriven; camera PWDN stays low; XCLK/RESET/SIOC use active outputs on an inout bus. HEX0..2 are explicitly off, VGA_SYNC is unused low, KEY2/3 and SW0..4 are unused. These warnings do not establish electrical connection correctness, which requires board verification.
NUM_PARALLEL_PROCESSORS not specified: performance/shared-host warning only. No global setting changed during active fitting.

metastability.actualReportFinding: map.rpt has no Synchronizer Summary/MTBF report or explicit custom-chain panel. SYNCHRONIZER_IDENTIFICATION source assignments occur only on Intel ISSP metastable_l1/l2 registers. The synthesis setting Synchronization Register Chain Length is 3. No custom chain removal appears in Registers Removed During Synthesis, but that absence does not prove post-fit chain placement or MTBF.
metastability.supportedAttributeEvidence: Intel altera_std_synchronizer.v lines45,47 use altera_attribute with SYNCHRONIZER_IDENTIFICATION FORCED_IF_ASYNCHRONOUS, DONT_MERGE_REGISTER ON and PRESERVE_REGISTER ON on both first and later stages.
metastability.helpConclusion: AUTO identifies possible chains but computes no MTBF. FORCED_IF_ASYNCHRONOUS or targeted FORCED enables MTBF reporting and, with OPTIMIZE_FOR_METASTABILITY ON, fitter optimisation. Attribute changes require refit. Forced must never be applied globally.
targetStages: heldBusCdc: requestSync[0:1] and acknowledgeSync[0:1] in requestCdc/resultToCamera/resultToDisplay
metastability.nextVerification: After refit, report_metastability with enough nchains and verify each expected custom chain has exactly two physical stages and non-negative settling slack. Check that constraints cause FORCED_IF_ASYNCHRONOUS to recognise all actual crossings; use narrowly targeted FORCED only if a real missed chain is demonstrated. Inspect chain-specific toggle-rate assumptions before making an MTBF claim. Current installed option help has an outdated family list omitting Cyclone V; actual post-fit report is required rather than inferring support from that list.

limitations: This is map-stage audit, not final Fitter/timing or hardware acceptance.
No numerical MTBF has been computed for this build.
FIFO read/write collision exclusion assumes common reset epoch and no illegal read/write; RTL simulation cannot model analogue metastability.
VGA single-buffer tearing is intentionally not eliminated.
The SCCB master cannot read back sensor registers.
Snapshot timeout output is dangling in this build; host sees a bounded missing-ready timeout, not a direct FPGA timeout status bit.
